 Comments by V. Pronyaev to the revision of ENDF/B-VII.1: 125 1451 12 
 1H(n,n) is a basic standard and at least the central values of 125 1451 13 
 this cross section should be the same in all libraries. 125 1451 14 
 G. Hale R-matrix (EDA) evaluation for ENDF/B-VII.1 evaluated for 125 1451 15 
 standards was taken as a base for one correction. It concerns the 125 1451 16 
 uncertainty of the standard. 125 1451 17 
 Original EDA (calculations) of CS uncertainties from uncertaint. 125 1451 18 
 of adjusted parameters gives extremely low uncertainties because 125 1451 19 
 normalization of experimental data in the fit are considered as 125 1451 20 
 free. Then due to strong cancellation of statistical 125 1451 21 
 uncertainties we have very low total evaluated uncertainties. 125 1451 22 
 In 2008 the procedure of calculations of covariance matrices of 125 1451 23 
 from covariance matrix of parameters was changed, and as result 125 1451 24 
 the total evaluated uncertainties are substantially larger 125 1451 25 
 CSEWG (1991) experts estimation of total uncertainty for 1H(n,n). 125 1451 26 
 Unfortunately CSEWG had not prepared the covariance (correlation) 125 1451 27 
 matrix, but consider CSEWG estimates as only statistical is not 125 1451 28 
 right. 125 1451 29 
 This file contains in MF=33, MT=2 the CSEWG (1991) percent 125 1451 30 
 estimates of total uncertainties and covariance matrix, obtained 125 1451 31 
 from 2 components - statistical and systematical fully correlated 125 1451 32 
 in all energy range - 1.0e-5 eV to 20 MeV. Systematical 125 1451 33 
 was taken equalto 0.18% what is at 0.02% below total in low- 125 1451 34 
 energy part where because of 1/v dependence and large number of 125 1451 35 
 points the uncertainties are minimal. The obtained covariance 125 1451 36 
 matrix is semi-positive and has three 0 eigenvalues 125 1451 37 
**************************************************************** 125 1451 38 
The new R-matrix analysis of the N-N system on which the ENDF/B- 125 1451 39 
VII evaluation for 1H is based differs from the previous one use 125 1451 40 
for ENDF/B-VI in several respects. Firstly, the n-p capture 125 1451 41 
reaction (MT=102), and its inverse, deuteron photo- 125 1451 42 
disintegration, were a part of the analysis, rather than added 125 1451 43 
later as before. The analysis used a new method for including 125 1451 44 
photon channels in R-matrix theory [1], which gave a better 125 1451 45 
description of the E1 transitions, in particular. The data for 125 1451 46 
these reactions are mostly integrated and differential cross 125 1451 47 
sections, but some information about polarizations was also 125 1451 48 
included. The thermal capture cross section was taken to be 125 1451 49 
332.0 mb, as was the recommendation from preliminary data 125 1451 50 
testing. Good agreement was obtained with recent cross-section 125 1451 51 
measurements [2,3] by astrophysical groups in the 20-550 keV 125 1451 52 
range, as well as with earlier measurements that had been done 125 1451 53 
mostly as photo-disintegration experiments at energies below 14 125 1451 54 
MeV. 125 1451 55 
The new analysis includes several additional measurements of the 125 1451 56 
total cross section (MT=1). The evaluated cross section 125 1451 57 
deviates at most by about -0.5% around 10 MeV from that of 125 1451 58 
ENDF/B-VI. The estimated uncertainty of the MT=1 cross section 125 1451 59 
is given at 2 MeV steps in the following table: 125 1451 60

For n-p scattering (MT=2), new information was included about the 125 1451 74 
low-energy cross sections (MF=3) and about the angular 125 1451 75 
distributions (MF=4). A new measurement of the angular 125 1451 76 
distribution at 10 MeV [4], plus corrections to earlier data at 125 1451 77 
14 MeV, moved the back-angle asymmetry in the 10-14 MeV range to 125 1451 78 
values that lie between those obtained for ENDF/B-V and ENDF/B- 125 1451 79 
VI. The addition of the latest value of the thermal coherent 125 1451 80 
scattering length [5] had the interesting effect of reducing the 125 1451 81 
"zero-energy" scattering cross section somewhat to agree 125 1451 82 
perfectly with an earlier measurement by Houk [6], and disagree 125 1451 83 
with the later, more precise, value of Dilg [7]. The 125 1451 84 
covariances for MT=2 will be added later, but the uncertainties 125 1451 85 
on the integrated cross section should be similar to those 125 1451 86 
listed above for the total cross section. 125 1451 87

[7] W. Dilg, Phys. Rev. C 11, 103 (1975). 125 1451 100 
 **************************************************************** 125 1451 101 
 125 1451 102 
Covariances were adopted from COMMARA-2.0 library in July 2011. 125 1451 103 
These covariances were obtained at LANL by full scale R-matrix 125 1451 104 
analysis of more than 5000 experimental data (chi-square/degree 125 1451 105 
of freedom of 0.83). [1] The major channel in this case is elastic 125 1451 106 
scattering, often labeled also as ''n-p'' scattering. Elastic 125 1451 107 
scattering serves as neutron cross section standard from 1 keV to 125 1451 108 
20 MeV, with cross sections well determined. Uncertainties for 125 1451 109 
elastic scattering rise from values well below 1%, reach maximum 125 1451 110 
at about 8 MeV, then gradually decrease with increasing energy. 125 1451 111 
In addition to elastic scattering, covariances are supplied for 125 1451 112 
radiative capture. 125 1451 113 
 125 1451 114

#### Covariances by material

#### Methodology

Thermal and Resonance Region

• Source of data 
• Experiments 
• ENDF file (retroactive method) 
• Atlas of Neutron Resonances (ANR) 
• SAMMY analysis 
• full analysis (MF32, Exp. data) 
• retroactive (MF32, ENDF file) 
• EMPIRE Resonance Module (MF32, ANR, scattering radius and thermal point uncertainties reproduced through correlations (if possible) 
• “Kernel Approximation” (MF33, ANR)

• ‘low-fidelity’ (Mark Williams) solution 
• Assimilation 

Fast neutron range (MF33)

• EMPIRE/KALMAN considering experimental data 
• Least Square fitting of experimental data (SOK code) 
• EMPIRE/KALMAN without experimental data (Low-Fidelity) 
• Dispersion analysis - differences among evaluations (and exp. data) 
• Reconsider previous work (ENDF/B VI.8, Low-Fidelity) 
• Visual analysis of experimental data 
• Assimilation

...

#### BNL additions

Major focus at BNL has been the adoption of AFCI/COMMARA covariance data

Most materials in COMMARA library had no covariance data in VII.0 and the (mostly MF33) covariances were moved directly

A few materials contained new MF32 covariances which required special handling: 50,52,53Cr and 58,60Ni.

#### Additional modifications...

• Zr isotopes: New BNL eval with total modulated following VI.8, JENDL-4 ang dist. for elastic. Modified thermal capture for Zr-90. 
• Standards covariances adopted for 6Li, 10B, 197Au, 237U, 238U, 239Pu. Uncertainties increased to cover dispersion, where necessary. 
• Many more minor fixes & updates.

Title: A Study of the Covariance Data in ENDF/B VIII.0 for Low Z Isotopes
URL: https://www.epj-conferences.org/articles/epjconf/pdf/2023/10/epjconf_nd2023_13002.pdf
Published: N/A
Author: Parsons D. Kent
Highlights:
## A Study of the Covariance Data in ENDF/B VIII.0 for Low Z

## Isotopes

D. Kent Parsons 1,*

1Nuclear Data Team, Group XCP-5, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos NM, USA

Abstract. Thirty group covariance data have been produced from ENDF/B VIII.0 MF 33 for H1, H2, He4, Li6, Li7, Be9, B10, B11, C12, C13, N15, O16, the JENDL O16 and F19. Multi-group cross section covariance data was produced by NJOY routine ERRORR. Negative eigenvalues were found only for F19, but the covariance constraints required for the condition of the sum of partial cross sections being equal to the resultant total cross section were found to be incorrect for H2, Li6, B10, C12, C13, and O16. An easy correction is suggested for Li6 and C13. An expansion of the ENDF-6 formats manual is suggested for the MF 33 chapter and a new proposed covariance normalization scheme is proposed.

### 1 Introduction

Thirty group covariance data have been produced for analysis and checking for H1, H2, He4, Li6, Li7, Be9, B10, B11, C12, C13, N15, O16, JENDL O16 and F19. (H3, He3, Be7, N14, O17, and O18 do not have any covariance data.) In processing these ENDF/B VIII.0 evaluations, cross section covariance data was produced from the data given in the MF 33 section. NJOY [1] routine ERRORR produces the multi-group covariances.

The standard Los Alamos “td” weighting function was used in the group collapse to 30 groups. Experience has shown that NJOY does not add any large negative eigenvalues while processing, though it can add some extra 0.0 eigenvalues. The 0.0 eigenvalues may assume small negative values due to numerical round-off.

The ENDF/B-VIII.1 release is the newest evaluated nuclear data library produced, distributed, and recommended by CSEWG for use in nuclear science and technology applications. Among the many key advances, relative to the previous version ENDF/B-VIII.0, are: re-evaluation of 239Pu file by a joint international effort; updated 16,18O, 19F, 28-30Si, 50-54Cr, 55Mn, 54,56,57Fe, 63,65Cu, 139La, 233,235,238U, and 240,241Pu neutron nuclear data by the IAEA-coordinated INDEN collaboration; significant changes for 3He, 6Li, 9Be, 51V, 88Sr, 103Rh, 140,142Ce, Dy, 181Ta, Pt, 206-208Pb, and 234,236U neutron data; new nuclear data for the photo-nuclear, being 196 adopted from the IAEA2019 Photonuclear Data Library and one new file from JENDL-5; and new evaluations for the charged-particle and atomic sublibraries. Numerous thermal neutron scattering kernels were re-evaluated or provided for the very first time. Additionally, new covariance testing was implemented. ENDF/B-VIII.1 reduced bias in the simulations of many integral experiments with particular progress noted for fluorine, copper and stainless steel containing benchmarks. Data issues which had hindered the deployment of ENDF/B-VIII.0 for commercial nuclear power applications in high burn-up situations, were addressed. ENDF/B-VIII.1 data are distributed in both ENDF-6 and GNDS formats.

The ENDF/B-VIII.1 library is the newest recommended evaluated nuclear data file by the Cross Section Evaluation Working Group (CSEWG) for use in nuclear science and technology applications, and incorporates advances made in the six years since the release of ENDF/B-VIII.0. Among key advances made are that the 239Pu file was reevaluated by a joint international effort and that updated 16,18O, 19F, 28− 30Si, 50− 54Cr, 55Mn, 54,56,57Fe, 63,65Cu, 139La, 233,235,238U, and 240,241Pu neutron nuclear data from the IAEA coordinated INDEN collaboration were adopted. Over 60 neutron dosimetry cross sections were adopted from the IAEA’s IRDFF-II library. In addition, the new library includes significant changes for 3He, 6Li, 9Be, 51V, 88Sr, 103Rh, 140,142Ce, Dy, 181Ta, Pt, 206− 208Pb, and 234,236U neutron data, and new nuclear data for the photonuclear, charged particle and atomic sublibraries. Numerous thermal neutron scattering kernels were reevaluated or provided for the very first time. On the covariance side, work was undertaken to introduce better uncertainty quantification standards and testing for nuclear data covariances. The significant effort to reevaluate important nuclides has reduced bias in the simulations of many integral experiments with particular progress noted for fluorine, copper, and stainless steel containing benchmarks. Data issues hindered the successful deployment of the previous ENDF/B-VIII.0 for commercial nuclear power applications in high burnup situations. These issues were addressed by improving the 238U and 239,240,241Pu evaluated data in the resonance region. The new library performance as a function of burnup is similar to the reference ENDF/B-VII.1 library. The ENDF/B-VIII.1 data are available in ENDF-6 and GNDS format at https://doi.org/10.11578/endf/2571019.
